articles.title: Cuttack Traffic Relief: Two Major Ring Road Stretches to Be Expanded to Six Lanes
articles.description: #ଦ ୂର_ହେବ_କଟକ_ଟ୍ରାଫିକ_ସମସ୍ୟା #୬_ଲ େନ୍_ହେବ.... କଟକ ସହରର ଟ୍ରାଫିକ ସମସ୍ୟା ଦୂର କରିବାକୁ ବଡ଼ ପଦକ୍ଷେପ । ସହରର ରିଂ ରୋଡ୍ ର ଆଉ ଦୁଇଟି ପ୍ରମୁଖ ରାସ୍ତା ହେବ ୬ ଲେନ୍ । ବେଲିଭ୍ୟୁ ଛକରୁ ଚହଟା ଏବଂ ନେତାଜୀ ସୁଭାଷ ସେତୁରୁ ନରାଜ ବ୍ରଜବିହାରୀପୁର ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ରାସ୍ତାର ହେବ ସମ୍ପ୍ରସାରଣ। ଏନେଇ ଟେଣ୍ଡରକୁ ସରକାର ଅନୁମୋଦନ ଦେଇଥିବା ବେଳେ ୫୦ କୋଟି ଟଙ୍କା ବ୍ୟୟରେ ୨ ବର୍ଷ ଭିତରେ କାମ ଶେଷ ହେବ ବୋଲି ଧାର୍ଯ୍ୟ ରଖାଯାଇଛି। In a major step towards easing traffic congestion in Cuttack, the Odisha Government has approved the tender for widening two key stretches of the city's Ring Road to six lanes. articles.title: Rising Salandi River puts Bhadrak villages on edge as flood threat returns
articles.description: Fresh concern gripped residents of Odisha’s Bhadrak district as the water level of the Salandi River began rising again on Thursday following continuous rainfall in the upper catchment areas, raising fears of another spell of flooding in low-lying villages. Also Read: ‘Crops rotting under water for weeks’: Back-to-back floods shatter farmers’ hopes in Odisha’s Bhadrak According to official data, the river was flowing at 16.30 feet at Rajghat today, just below the ‘danger mark’ of 17 feet. The rising water level has once again threatened vulnerable settlements that were only beginning to recover from the previous flood. Floodwater measuring nearly two feet continues to flow over the bridge connecting Talagopabindha and Tiadi Sahi, disrupting movement and leaving several villages, including Narasinghpur, Tiadi Sahi, Sial Sahi, Matagajapur, Hatanagar and Nithapada, cut off from the rest of the district. Residents said they have remained in isolation for more than a week, with access to markets and essential supplies becoming increasingly difficult. Many villagers expressed anxiety over the renewed rise in the river, saying water had started receding briefly before heavy rainfall upstream caused it to swell again. They fear that continued rainfall could worsen the situation and inundate more habitations. Residents also voiced concern over debris accumulating around the bridge, warning that it could obstruct the river’s flow and increase pressure on the structure. They urged the administration to closely monitor the situation and expedite the construction of a new bridge promised for the area. With the river continuing to rise, people remain on alert, hoping the water level stabilises before it crosses the ‘danger mark’ and triggers fresh flooding. “This is Talagopabindha panchayat. Currently, there is about 2 to 2.5 feet of water on the bridge over the Nalia river. There are two Wards on the other side. In these two Wards, there are at least 500 people. They are currently living in fear due to the rising water. Whatever food they are getting, or what is being provided by the government, they are managing with that. Now that the water has risen again, only God knows what will happen,” a resident told OTV. “If you go into the village, there is a strong current. We are sitting on the porch with our children. The water is rising very fast. It has risen this much since morning. Those who are risking their lives are going to the shops, but even shops don’t have everything,” an elderly villager expressed. “If they bring puffed rice, there is no flattened rice, and if they bring flattened rice, there is something else missing. Where will they go in such a situation when the floodwater has submerged everywhere?” the elderly man further said. “Two days ago, the water level had receded a bit. The flood from four days ago had receded, giving people some relief. But now, the water is rising again. The way the water is rising, the most dangerous thing is the logs and debris getting stuck. The bridge might break. We have informed the administration many times,” a third villager stated. “However, Minister Suryabanshi Suraj is from this constituency, and he has promised us that an estimate of Rs 3.20 crore has been made for a new bridge. We hope that the Minister will float the tender soon and a new bridge will be built,” the young man added.

articles.title: OPINION | Zuckerberg apology: Power of India's law
articles.description: The written apology tendered to the Government of India by Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg is a clear reflection of the power of Indian laws. articles.title: Four in five MSMEs expect digital procurement to drive growth
articles.description: From digital payments to online shopping, India's digital transformation has largely focussed on consumers. The India MSME Digital Procurement Report 2026 suggests businesses are now increasingly looking at procurement as another area where digital tools could improve efficiency and support growth. Procurement covers the process of sourcing goods and services—from identifying suppliers and comparing prices to placing orders and managing deliveries.The report, released by the India SME Forum (ISF) in partnership with Amazon Business on Thursday, is bas¬ed on a survey of more than 27,000 Udyam-registered MSMEs across manufacturing, services and trading sectors. It estimates that India's MSME procurement economy is currently worth Rs124.9 trillion, making it one of the country's largest business expenditure categories. Yet only 30 to 40 percent of procurement spending currently happens through digital channels, according to the report, even as 80 percent, or four out of five, surveyed businesses said they expect digital procurement to play a major role in expanding their operations over three years.According to the Ministry of MSME's Annual Report 2025-26, the sector contributes around 31.1 percent of India's GDP, accounts for more than 48.5 percent of exports and is the country's second-largest source of employment after agriculture. Those numbers make procurement a significant cost centre for a large part of the economy.The survey was released a day after Parliament passed the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026. The Bill introduces a national digital registration platform for MSMEs, mandates invoice settlement through the Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) for central public sector enterprises procuring from MSMEs, and expands the use of online mediation and dispute resolution.Vinod Kumar, president of India SME Forum, says the amendments largely formalise reforms introduced over the past six to seven years through executive notifications by incorporating them into the MSMED Act. "Every business succeeds by increasing the gap between its input costs and its selling price. While considerable attention has traditionally been given to helping MSMEs increase revenues, far less attention has been paid to reducing procurement costs," Kumar tells Forbes India.According to the survey, price volatility is the biggest procurement challenge for MSMEs, cited by 55.7 percent of respondents, followed by managing multiple suppliers (37.6 percent), payment and credit constraints (35.6 percent) and the absence of a dependable vendor (33.4 percent).When choosing digital procurement platforms, businesses said flexible payment and credit facilities (49.9 percent), GST-compliant invoicing (45 percent), wider product selection (43.3 percent), ease of ordering (43.1 percent) and faster delivery (40.3 percent) were among the most important considerations.Mitranjan Bhaduri, director of Amazon Business India, says the report highlights an often-overlooked aspect of MSME digitisation. "Traditionally, procurement has been viewed as a cost centre. However, the ISF report demonstrates that procurement can become a strategic competitive advantage. Digital procurement allows businesses to source from a much wider network of verified suppliers, compare prices transparently and receive dependable deliveries. This creates efficiencies that directly improve profitability," he tells Forbes India.Bhaduri adds that GST compliance has also become an important consideration for businesses moving procurement online.GST-compliant invoicing has become increasingly vital since India began rolling out mandatory e-invoicing under the GST regime in phases from October 2020. The requirement was extended to businesses with annual turnover above Rs5 crore in August 2023"Businesses should not have to spend time chasing suppliers for invoices or resolving GST compliance issues. Through Amazon Business, invoices follow a standardised format and transaction information is integrated with the government's invoice registration systems, making it significantly easier for businesses to claim GST input credits and manage compliance," Bhaduri says.Aside from Amazon Business, the report found MSMEs also use platforms such as Moglix, OfBusiness, IndustryBuying, IndiaMART, Flipkart Business, Udaan and Jumbotail for different procurement needs.Speaking at the report's launch, Minister of State for MSME Shobha Karandlaje said, "As businesses increasingly adopt digital technologies, procurement too must evolve from a routine operational function into a strategic business capability. Digital procurement can help MSMEs improve efficiency, reduce costs, access wider markets and build stronger supply chains, enabling them to compete more effectively in India and globally."Around 61.5 percent of surveyed MSMEs said they plan to increase their use of digital procurement tools, while nearly half expect to adopt artificial intelligence-powered procurement solutions over the next two years, according to the report.The survey, however, covers only Udyam-registered MSMEs. Kumar estimated that another six to seven crore enterprises continue to operate outside the formal system. He believes that many either perceive registration as increasing compliance obligations or do not yet see sufficient incentives to register. That leaves open the question of how quickly digital procurement can extend beyond registered businesses to the wider informal MSME ecosystem.

articles.title: Delhi Health dept report finds ‘no overpricing’ in procurement
articles.description: A report submitted by the Delhi health department to the city government’s Directorate of Vigilance has found no evidence of overpricing in the procurement of medicines, medical equipment and hospital supplies, arguing that official procurement records show several purchases by the government’s Central Procurement Agency (CPA) were made at rates comparable to, or lower than, those paid by other government institutions across the country
